page: Amazon Web Services i8g.4xlarge is a storage-optimized server powered by custom AWS Graviton Neoverse-V2 processors built on the arm64 architecture. It features 16 dedicated physical cores and 16 vCPUs running at 2.8 GHz, paired with 128.0 GB of system memory, which provides 8.0 GB of RAM per core. The instance is equipped with 3750 GB of bundled local NVMe SSD storage and a baseline network bandwidth of 9 Gbps, running on the AWS Nitro hypervisor.

Benchmark data highlights strong memory performance, with a Passmark memory score in the top 10% and uncached large-block memory read bandwidth reaching 296.95 GB/sec, placing it in the top 25%. Multi-threaded bzip3 decompression and Passmark database operations also rank in the top 25%, demonstrating efficient data processing capabilities. However, CPU-based LLM inference performance is limited, with text generation on a medium 7B model averaging 16.71 tokens/sec and large 70B models dropping to 2.29 tokens/sec.

The arm64 architecture and dedicated core allocation provide high resource density and qualitative cost efficiency for I/O-intensive operations. The combination of high-capacity local NVMe storage and strong memory bandwidth makes this instance highly suitable for transactional databases, caching layers, data indexing, and high-throughput storage workloads.
